title: Hosted and Freestanding C Implementations and Portability
learningObjectives: Distinguish hosted and freestanding C implementation environments at a high level.
Explain why hosted programs commonly use main and standard library facilities while freestanding environments may provide different startup and library support.
Identify platform assumptions involving compiler, target architecture, operating system, ABI and available libraries.
Separate ISO C guarantees from implementation-defined behavior, unspecified behavior and compiler extensions.
Write portable code by using standard interfaces, documenting assumptions and testing on the intended target.

understand.concept: C can be implemented in different execution environments. A hosted implementation provides the facilities required for a hosted environment, including conventional program startup that calls main and a specified set of standard library facilities. A freestanding implementation is intended for environments where a complete hosted environment may not exist, such as some embedded or kernel development contexts; startup and available library facilities differ. Portability depends on distinguishing what ISO C guarantees from implementation choices and target-specific facilities.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding Hosted and freestanding implementations; target environment and portability (CodeSaathi extension) helps you reason about program behaviour instead of memorizing syntax. It is useful in exams, debugging and building reliable C applications.
understand.analogy: Treat the concept as a tool with a precise contract: it has valid inputs, defined operations and observable results.
understand.analogyLimit: An analogy is only an aid; the C standard and the relevant function specifications determine actual behaviour.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Hosted environments

A hosted C environment is the common model for desktop and server applications. The implementation provides hosted startup and required standard library facilities. A typical hosted program defines int main(void) or another permitted form of main, and the runtime environment calls it to begin program execution.

## 2. Freestanding environments

A freestanding environment may be used where there is no conventional operating-system process model or hosted runtime. Examples include some embedded systems, firmware and operating-system components. Startup code, entry point and available library facilities can differ from a hosted application. Do not assume every hosted library service is available.

## 3. Target environment matters

A compiler targets a combination of processor architecture, operating environment and application binary interface (ABI). The target affects executable format, calling conventions, available system services and sometimes the sizes or representations of C types. A program built for one target is not automatically executable on another.

## 4. Portable C and implementation choices

C standardizes language rules, but some properties are implementation-defined or unspecified. The exact width of many integer types is not universally fixed. Use sizeof, limits from limits.h and fixed-width integer types from stdint.h when their requirements fit the task. Avoid undefined behavior and undocumented compiler extensions.

## 5. Choose the right assumptions

Record the compiler and version, target architecture, operating environment, language standard mode and required libraries. Compile and test on the actual target or a representative toolchain. Cross-compilation can build for a different target, but it does not replace target-device testing.

examples.title: Inspect properties of the current implementation
examples.explanation: This hosted example reports properties of the implementation used to build and run it. The values should not be assumed identical on every C implementation.

examples.title: Use a fixed-width integer type when appropriate
examples.explanation: When the implementation provides uint32_t, the matching PRIu32 macro supplies the correct printf format. Exact-width typedefs are optional when an implementation cannot support the exact width.

practise.guidedTask: Record whether your development environment is hosted or freestanding. Identify its compiler, target architecture, operating environment and available libraries. Build a small program using facilities supported by that environment.
practise.independentTask: Compare the assumptions made by a desktop C program and a small embedded target. Identify which assumptions concern ISO C and which depend on the platform. Document the target and test using its supported toolchain.
hints: Hosted and freestanding describe execution environments, not skill levels.
The availability of standard library facilities differs by environment.
A target includes more than the source language.
Implementation-defined choices should be documented by the implementation.
Test on the actual supported target whenever possible.
